_doc: DRAFT — NOT SUBMITTED. The values a prefix.cc registration for this vocabulary would carry, written down so the submission is a copy-paste rather than a decision made at the form. Nothing here has been filed: prefix.cc holds no VSON entry, this project claims no registration, and no automated process may create one. Filing is a person's act, done by the maintainer under their own identity. This file is the record of the drafted values and of what was verified when — update `status`, `submitted`, `submitted_at` and `submitted_by` on the day it is actually filed, and re-run `make site`.

registry.name: prefix.cc
registry.scope: prefix.cc binds one short prefix to one namespace URI. It is a convenience lookup, not an authority: nothing in VSON depends on it, and a document that binds any other prefix to the namespace below is exactly as conformant.

declared_in.note: The registration must repeat what the vocabulary already publishes. If these two ever disagree, the Turtle is right and this file is stale.

why_not_vso: `vso` — the prefix every Turtle document in this repository writes, and the one this vocabulary published until 2026-07-31 — is already the Vehicle Sales Ontology's. Registering it would ask consumers to rebind a prefix a decade-old published vocabulary holds, and a graph mixing the two vocabularies could not bind both. `vson` is unambiguous, matches the notation's name and the w3id path, and costs nothing to adopt: a prefix binding is an abbreviation the parser expands away, so no IRI, no document and no fixture changes. tests/test_prefix_binding.py holds that invariant; docs/vson.md §5.1 states the decision.

no_iri_change.note: Byte-identical. This change moves a published hint about a name, never a name.

evidence.claim: The prefix `vso` is already published for a different vocabulary.
evidence.result: Vehicle Sales Ontology (vso), namespace http://purl.org/vso/ns#, by Martin Hepp; the earliest version LOV lists is dated 2010-10-02.

evidence.claim: The prefix `vson` is unbound at prefix.cc.
evidence.method: Reported by the reviewer who raised the collision. An independent re-check the same day did not complete: prefix.cc refused the TLS handshake with an expired certificate (curl exit 60), over both plain curl and a fetch tool.
evidence.result: UNCONFIRMED from this checkout. The change to `vson` does not depend on it — an unregistered preferred prefix is still a preferred prefix — but the registration does.

recheck_before_filing: That https://prefix.cc/vson is still unbound, on a day prefix.cc serves a valid certificate.

not_submitted_here.note: The four companion namespaces keep the prefixes they already publish — they were not part of this collision, and none of them has been checked against a prefix registry. Any submission for them needs that check first.
